videos.script:
So far the planner has read one file, courses.json, and kept every change in memory. Real apps ask a server. This lesson's server speaks GraphQL.

{{schema}} GraphQL starts with a schema. A list of types, and the fields each one has. A course has a title and sessions. A session has a date, minutes, and whether it is done. Everything a client may ask for is in that file, and nothing else.

{{query}} A query is shaped like the answer. You name the fields you want, and the answer comes back with exactly those fields, nested the same way. Ask for a course's title and its sessions' dates, and that is all you get.

{{server}} You will run a small server of under fifty lines, built on the reference implementation, and ask it questions from the terminal. Then break one on purpose, because the way GraphQL reports an error is not the way HTTP does.

{{mutation}} Mutations change things, and return what they changed. Fragments give a set of fields a name, so two operations ask for the same shape.

{{planner}} Then the planner itself asks the server, and a test checks every query it sends against the schema, before anything runs.
